_budget_comment: PIXELS, measured - not characters, and not a guess. Every glyph in FONT.BIN carries its own advance (1..15 px at a 16 px cell), so the width of a shipped line is computable exactly: sum the advances of its characters. These are the widest line each family actually renders, which is the bound the skill asks for. 'default' is 382, the widest anything on the disc draws, on a 480 px screen. The earlier character-count capacity was an upper bound standing in for this until the font was read; these numbers replace it.
_budget_db_comment: The db__ families are DATABASE.DAT members: item and monster names, job and magic descriptions, the name-entry pools and the system string table. None of them is drawn in the dialogue box, so none may inherit its width. Each number here is that family s own widest shipped Japanese line, measured with the same per-glyph advances as every other entry - a LOWER BOUND on the real widget, since the game demonstrably drew that line. For these families the binding limit is usually not pixels at all but BYTES: a record-table string sits in a fixed-width field and cannot grow, which hanpatch/bytebudget.py enforces from work/db_budget.json.
_capacity_comment: Per-family maxima measured over 4587 shipped records. The widest the original ever renders in a family is the proven bound for that family; battle_info.dsf at 32 is the widest anything on the disc gets. These are CHARACTER counts against a proportional font, so they are an upper bound to be replaced by pixel measurement once the Korean font is built - a 32-character Korean line of full-width glyphs is wider than a 32-character Japanese one that mixes half-width kana.
_comment: Classic Dungeon X2 (PSP, Japan, v1.02). Every number here was measured from the disc and can be re-derived: capacity from the shipped corpus, font facts from the shipped font. Nothing is a preference. The game's text is not in this file - budgets are lengths, not strings.
_engine_wraps_comment: NOT MEASURED AT RUNTIME. 459 of 465 quoted records open and close their bracket inside one record, which is consistent with one record being one rendered line and not with the engine reflowing. Until the renderer is observed this stays a hypothesis and the capacity gate is the only bound.
_engine_wraps_families_comment: The executable is a SECOND container with the opposite layout property to the script, and the title-wide `engine_wraps: false` is wrong for it. Measured: EBOOT source lines reach 511px on a 480px screen, which cannot be one display line, so the engine wraps them; and its slots are NUL-terminated byte buffers overwritten whole, not fixed-line records. Under the title-wide rule three install messages were unstorable no matter what they said - the Japanese itself rewraps from 2 stored lines to 3 display lines. The real constraint on these rows is the byte budget, which bytebudget.py enforces from the slot length.
_font_charset_comment: Deliberately absent rather than 'ksx1001'. The font holds 3072 cells, the disc fills 2725, and only 1493 hold glyphs that neither the script nor the database renders, so 1493 cells can be retargeted. KS X 1001 needs 2350 and does not fit. The charset is DERIVED from the sealed translation by tools/cdx2_font.py and the build fails if the syllables it needs exceed the cells that are free.
_font_shade_comment: The 3DS titles need a shading LUT because their sheets are RGBA4444 with a shading mask multiplied against the text colour. This font does not: its 16-entry palette is a straight linear alpha ramp on white (index n is alpha 17n), measured off both shipped archives. The identity ramp recorded here IS that measurement - coverage maps to the palette index unchanged - not a default standing in for one.
_glossary_required_comment: Measured absence, not an omitted gate: this title has no name-key tables or fixed terms (terms={} and name_keys=[]), so glossary.build examines 0 source rows. The audit may report that explicit absence; any title without this declaration still fails closed on an empty glossary.
_glyph_authority_comment: Measured, not preferred. The renderer advances by scale*(advance+1) (EBOOT 0x1ddc0), so an advance of 0 still moves the cursor one pixel and jamo cannot be overlaid - compositional Hangul is impossible on this engine and every syllable needs its own cell. With 1840 cells against 11172 precomposed syllables the charset must be DERIVED from the translation, which makes a translation-time glyph filter circular: it was run that way and took three rebake rounds, each uncovering syllables the last font lacked. The authority moves to the build, where the font is baked from the shipped text and verify reads it back out of the ROM.
_latin_allow_comment: Classified by CONTEXT, not by shape. Every token above except LV, MML, O, T, SP and X appears only in rows that contain no Japanese at all - they are asset and animation references the engine resolves, not text a player reads, so translating them would break the reference. MML is the game's music-data format, O, T and X are parameter letters, and SP is a player-facing stat token; the source uses them as technical identifiers and the Korean policy preserves their ASCII spelling. Shape alone gets this wrong: CRITICAL, SELECT and OPENING are all-caps like the identifiers, but CRITICAL and SELECT occur INSIDE Japanese prose and are therefore labels a Korean player should read in Korean, while OPENING occurs only in ASCII-only rows. LV is the one policy call: a level abbreviation Korean RPGs conventionally keep. The remaining English words in the corpus - CRITICAL, SELECT, Music, Macro, Language, Invalidity, JobSkill - are deliberately NOT allowed, because leaving them is a translation that did not happen. CRT and SPD are the game's own stat abbreviations - critical rate and speed - and appear 19 and 10 times in weapon and shield help text beside ATK, DEF, HP and EXP, which the built-in allowance already covers. The shipped Japanese writes them in Latin, so a correct Korean rendering must keep them; without the allowance every '歩き-10 CRT+3' row was rejected as untranslated Latin. L joins O and T on the same evidence: they are the MML parameter letters, and the three rows are the music-editor key help - Ｏ：オクターブを指定, Ｔ：テンポ指定, Ｌ：音の長さ指定. O and T were listed and L was not, so the L row was the only one of the three the copied-span rule refused. KB is a unit symbol like SP: it appears inside Japanese prose and a Korean reader reads it as KB.
_register_default_comment: Measured, and the measurement is why it is 'plain' rather than 'polite'. Register splits by bucket on this disc: UI/system families lean polite 370 to 174, story families lean plain 242 to 84. register_default only governs records that declare no marker, and those 3717 records are 64.7% story - the bucket that is plain-dominant. So the default follows the majority of the text it actually governs, and the polite UI families are handled by their own register entries rather than by flipping the global value.
_tag_pattern_comment: Measured, not assumed. The script domain contains no markup at all - no <>, {}, [], @-token or %-escape - and for that domain alone '(?!)' (a regex matching nothing) was the truthful recogniser. The DATABASE domain, added later, does use C printf specifiers: 97 rows across STRTBL, JOB and JOBSKILL, in exactly 14 forms (%s %d %2d %4d %02d %-2d %3d %6d %2s %-3.1f %3s %9d %7s %-12s). Leaving them unrecognised was not cosmetic: they survive tokenisation as the words 's', 'exp' and '6d', so copied_spans saw every correct translation of '%s\n%EXP%6d' as source copied verbatim and rejected all 32 outstanding STRTBL rows - a rule no translation could satisfy without corrupting the format string. The pattern is deliberately restricted to the conversions this disc uses; a bare '%' followed by text is a literal percent sign here ('%1', '%2', '%ま', '%確', '%Ｅ') and must stay text.
_voice_authority_comment: precedent_backed cannot be used by anyone right now: the shipped catalogue is canonical 0 of 10, so no type can back a sealed contract. That is the tool's honest state, not a blocker to route around.
_voice_contract_comment: hancharacter measured and the floor is not met, which is reported rather than worked around. The corpus carries no speaker-attribution surface: 459 of 465 quoted records are self-contained and only 48 have a speaker-shaped predecessor, so there is nothing to segment a contract by. Catalogue role-language markers are absent at any density worth sealing - the largest is ja_elder_lexicon at 25 of 4587 records and it clusters in battle_info.dsf, which is system text, not a character. Every other type matches 1 or 2 records, which is noise. Sealing a contract here would manufacture a voice the source does not have, which hancharacter classifies as INVENTION. Mode is prose_fidelity and density is report-only.
budget_measured: NOT a measured box. These are the widest line each family actually renders, computed from the shipped text and the font's own per-glyph advances (1-15px at a 16px cell, EBOOT renderer steps scale*(advance+1)). The container drew those lines, so each number is a LOWER BOUND on its box: using it as the budget can only be tighter than the truth, never looser, so it cannot let overflow through. The real box width needs a screenshot from a running renderer and has not been taken; when it is, these numbers should be replaced and this note rewritten rather than kept alongside a measurement it no longer describes.
_budget_is_lower_bound_comment: The machine-readable half of budget_measured. Those numbers are the widest line each family renders, not the width of a box, so a family budget is the widest ROW anywhere in the family and proves nothing about the slot an individual row draws in. Declaring this sends every row that carries its own line break through wrap.row_layout, which measures it against its own source lines. Found by playing the 23:17 build: db__STRTBL.DAT/s22 draws 2 lines of at most 267px and its Korean shipped as one 459px line on a 480px screen, clipped at both edges, with the family check clean because db__STRTBL.DAT runs to ~800px elsewhere.
